gaps.sentence: ___ of the two passwords works — try the other one.
gaps.hint: not one and not the other
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' = not either of them.

gaps.sentence: The plane had no ___ taken off than the captain was forced to turn back.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner … than' is the fixed pair; here it sits after 'had'.

gaps.sentence: We stopped ___ some photos on the way.
gaps.explanation: 'stop to do' = pause in order to do something.

gaps.sentence: They marched through the capital ___ protest.
gaps.explanation: 'In protest' = as a way of protesting.

gaps.sentence: The committee meets ___ other month, always on a Tuesday.
gaps.explanation: 'Every other month' = one month yes, one month no.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ he finished speaking when the audience erupted.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly' at the front inverts the past perfect: Hardly had he finished… when…
'Pride oneself on something' is the reflexive collocation (formal 'upon' is also possible).

gaps.sentence: It was ___ a good film that we saw it twice.
